reason: The two conversions between an exact fraction and a double (`toDouble`, `exactDouble` in src/model/rational.ts) do less work for the same result: `toDouble` finds its exponent from two digit counts and divides once, where it multiplied by 10 and divided about 26 times; `exactDouble` drops the mantissa's trailing zero bits, where it ran Euclid's algorithm on a power of two. Every result is the one the earlier forms gave, which are kept in src/model/rationalConversions.test.ts as the reference and compared over the ends of the range, the boundaries, the ties, decimals past both ends, the values a document holds and random fractions and doubles. No value a document computes, stores or shows changes; stepping and Monte Carlo runs take less time, most where a document has units.
